articles.title: Euro zone growth beats projections again
Euro Zone Growth Beats Projections but Headwinds Mount
articles.description: Thirdquarter growth of 0.4 beats expectations for 0.2 in poll Inflation rising in most big euro zone countries Unemployment is holding steady Further interest rate hike seen as almost certain FRANKFURT, Oct 30 Reuters The euro zone economy grew faster than predicted last quarter, displaying exceptional resilience to headwinds from expensive energy, even as surging borrowing costs and rapid inflation cloud the outlook. The euro zone economy has beaten most estimates this year, expanding steadily on the back of robust investment and consumption, confounding expectations for a downturn as energy price rises sap incomes. The economies of the 21 nations sharing the euro grew by 0.4 in the third quarter, a slowdown from an exceptionally strong 0.6 three months earlier, but far above expectations for 0.2 in a Reuters poll of economists. Compared with a year earlier, the bloc39;s economy grew by 1.3, beating expectations for 1.1, as heavy spending on AI, defence and infrastructure boosted investment, robust foreign demand helped industry, and households kept on spending, reducing their already high savings rate. Among the euro zone39;s biggest economies, Germany expanded by 0.2 on the quarter, Spain and the Netherlands by 0.6, while Italy was unchanged and the French economy contracted by 0.1. While the bloc39;s growth rate is less than half of the expansion produced by the United States, the figure far exceeds the gloomy projections made after the start of the Iran...

articles.title: Bulgarian Marine Drone for Autonomous Missions to Be Tested in Burgas Bay in Coming Weeks
articles.description: A marine drone designed for autonomous missions is to be tested in Burgas Bay, Helios Marine founder and CEO Dimitar Enchev told journalists ahead of the start of the Black Sea 2030: Security, Resilience, Innovation International Forum, taking place at the International Congress Centre in Burgas on Friday. The testing of the device will begin within two weeks in the Burgas Bay area. The drone is manufactured in Burgas and is an autonomous platform capable of moving independently, navigating and surveying coastal areas. Its capabilities depend on the equipment module fitted. A version for aerial missions has currently been developed, Enchev said. Potential applications for the platform include sample collection, the surveillance and tracking of enemy drones, surveying areas affected by oil spills, and search and rescue operations in rough waters. “We hope to put it into autonomous operation once it has passed certification. We have already held discussions with all the relevant institutions,” Enchev added.

articles.title: Where Did All the iPhone Duos Go? Mostly to Apple's Stores
articles.description: Apple allocated roughly 80% of its initial iPhone Duo inventory to its retail stores, with locations holding as few as 50 units each, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Speaking on the latest episode of his Power On podcast, Gurman, citing people very close to the device's logistics, said most customers who bought a Duo in store on day one got one by waiting in line. Flagship stores were said to have held up to around 250 units, and Fifth Avenue was stocked unusually heavily because Apple executives attended the launch. The inventory split helps explain why pre-orders slipped to late January within minutes on October 16, while most people who queued on launch day walked away with a new phone. At the time, Apple described demand as "nothing short of extraordinary" and said it was working to satisfy demand "as quickly as possible," so there's a good chance that, even if a delivery estimate for your order is way out in the future, it could improve over time. Where to Buy iPhone Duo: Stores, Pickup, and Wait Times Just Got an iPhone Duo? In the UK, the same storage tiers run £1,999, £2,199, £2,599, and £3,199 on Apple's UK store. articles.title: Apollo Silver delivers positive PEA for California project
articles.description: TSX-V-listed Apollo Silver Corp has reported positive results from a preliminary economic assessment (PEA) at its Calico silver project, California, in the US, with the PEA estimating an after-tax net present value (NPV) of $737-million, an after-tax internal rate of return of 25% and a payback period of three years. The PEA is based on the development of an openpit mining operation at the Waterloo deposit, feeding a conventional 8 000 t a day milling and cyanidation leach plant with an initial planned processing life of about 15 years.
